newsitem.title: USA: DeBakey sees rapid recovery for Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: DeBakey sees rapid recovery for Yeltsin.

text.p: Noted heart surgeon Michael DeBakey said on Wednesday he expected a quick recovery by Russian President Boris Yeltsin from what he said was likely a case of the flu.
DeBakey told Reuters Yeltsin was receiving antibiotics and should improve rapidly enough to go home from the hospital within "three days to a week."
Yeltsin, who had major heart surgery on Nov. 5, was taken to a hospital in Moscow on Wednesday for what was described as the early stages of pneumonia.

Debakey, who served as a consultant during the heart surgery, said Yeltsin's physician Renat Akchurin told him by telephone that X-rays had found a patch of "pneumonitis" or inflammation in his left lung but it had been caught early enough to keep it from developing into full-blown pneumonia.

"It sounds to me like it is the flu. There's a lot of it going around in Moscow these days," DeBakey said. He said Akchurin, who performed the heart operation, was not concerned about the president's illness.
"He didn't regard this as life-threatening at all and usually it isn't. Since (Yeltsin's) heart function is almost normal, he can be regarded as a normal person having the flu."
DeBakey, 88, told CNN the illness "has nothing to do with the heart operation. In fact he's really better off having the flu now after the operation than if he had the flu before."

Akchurin, a former student of DeBakey at Houston's Baylor College of Medicine, performed a quintuple bypass on Yeltsin to improve blood flow to his heart. Before the surgery, Yeltsin's heart, damaged from previous heart attacks, was in such poor condition that he had to put aside many of his duties and was not seen in public for many weeks.
He returned to work at the Kremlin in late December but on Monday the government said he had cancelled meetings this week because of what was described then as a "heavy cold."
News reports said Yeltsin appeared wan in recent days, but DeBakey attributed that to flu. "He's had the flu since over the weekend. If you'd had the flu, you know how it feels."
Despite the illness, DeBakey was optimistic about Yeltsin's long-term health prospects. "His general condition is very good," he said.
